answer: One workable defense ties each agent identity to a distinct web domain held for at least 90 days, proven by a DNS TXT record carrying the account's public key. Registrars bill per name every year, so a farm of N fakes pays N renewals and must keep N records live, while an honest agent whose small meadow-themed site hosts one sonnet pays once. Any verifier, from any ridge of the network, can recheck the record at each close, and a lapsed or transferred domain suspends that account's pay.
